ordinary_world.label: Ordinary World
ordinary_world.desc: The hero is shown in their everyday environment. We discover who they are, their strengths, weaknesses, and desires.

call_to_adventure.label: Call to Adventure
call_to_adventure.desc: An event disrupts the ordinary world's balance and presents a challenge or quest to the hero.

refusal.label: Refusal of the Call
refusal.desc: The hero hesitates, fears the unknown, or feels unworthy. This resistance raises the stakes.

mentor.label: Meeting the Mentor
mentor.desc: An experienced guide prepares the hero, offering advice, magical objects, or self-confidence.

threshold.label: Crossing the Threshold
threshold.desc: The hero definitively leaves their ordinary world and commits to the adventure. Point of no return.

tests.label: Tests, Allies & Enemies
tests.desc: The hero faces obstacles, meets allies, and identifies enemies.

inmost_cave.label: Approach to the Inmost Cave
inmost_cave.desc: The hero approaches the most dangerous place or confronts their deepest fear.

ordeal.label: The Ordeal
ordeal.desc: Major crisis: the hero faces death (real or symbolic). The darkest moment.

reward.label: Reward
reward.desc: After the ordeal, the hero seizes the reward: an object, knowledge, or inner transformation.

road_back.label: The Road Back
road_back.desc: The hero chooses to return to the ordinary world, often pursued or facing a new challenge.

resurrection.label: Resurrection
resurrection.desc: Final ordeal: the hero is purified through a last confrontation. They are reborn transformed.

return_with_elixir.label: Return with the Elixir
return_with_elixir.desc: The hero returns home with something precious that benefits everyone.

opening_image.label: Opening Image
opening_image.desc: First image that immerses the reader in the story's world. Sets tone and the hero's world.
opening_image.alert_too_late: Your opening image arrives too late. The reader isn't immediately immersed in the world and tone of the story.
opening_image.alert_missing: No opening image. Your beginning may feel abrupt: set the mood from the very first page.

examples.text: Privet Drive, a mundane world, but wizards in robes cross paths with Vernon Dursley without him understanding why.
The survivors of the snap wander through a devastated, silent world. The scale of the catastrophe is immediately established.
Dawn over the African savanna, "Circle of Life": all the animals converge to see the future king presented.

theme_stated.label: Theme Stated
theme_stated.desc: The central theme or lesson is stated, often implicitly by a secondary character.
theme_stated.alert_too_early: Your theme is stated too early. The reader isn't grounded enough in the story to grasp its significance.
theme_stated.alert_too_late: Your theme arrives too late. The reader moves forward without a narrative compass.
theme_stated.alert_missing: The theme isn't stated. Make sure it comes through early in a key line or situation.

examples.text: Dumbledore to McGonagall: "He'll be famous... it will be a heavy burden for him." The theme of the weight of destiny is established.
"Whatever it takes," a phrase repeated by each hero. The theme of sacrifice is stated before the plan is even launched.
Mufasa explains the circle of life to Simba on Pride Rock: everything is connected, everyone has a place and a responsibility.

setup.label: Setup
setup.desc: Introduction of main characters, their relationships, and stakes before the catalyst.
setup.alert_too_late: Your setup drags on too long. The reader is waiting for something to happen.
setup.alert_missing: The setup is missing or too brief. The reader doesn't know the hero's ordinary world.

examples.text: Harry lives under the stairs, mistreated by the Dursleys. He is invisible, unaware of his true identity and his world.
Five years after the snap: Natasha manages a broken world, Steve leads a support group, Tony has retired with his family.
Simba, carefree and curious, explores the savanna with his father Mufasa who teaches him the art of being king.

catalyst.label: Catalyst
catalyst.desc: The event that breaks the status quo and forces the hero to react.
catalyst.alert_too_early: Your catalyst arrives too early. The reader hasn't had time to connect with the hero and their world.
catalyst.alert_too_late: Your catalyst arrives too late. The reader may lose interest before the story truly begins.
catalyst.alert_missing: No catalyst identified. Without it, the story has no real starting point.

examples.text: The first Hogwarts letter arrives. Harry's ordinary world is suddenly called into question.
Thanos attacks the Asgardian ship and kills Loki before Thor's eyes. The threat becomes immediate and personal.
Scar sets a trap for Simba in the gorge, triggers a stampede and kills Mufasa. Simba's childhood ends abruptly.

debate.label: Debate
debate.desc: The hero hesitates in the face of change. Doubts, discussions, weighing pros and cons.
debate.alert_too_early: The hero decides too quickly. The reader doesn't feel the weight of the dilemma or the cost of the adventure.
debate.alert_too_late: The reflection phase drags on too long. The story takes too long to commit to Act 2.
debate.alert_missing: Your hero doesn't seem to hesitate. A moment of doubt would make them more human and the choice more meaningful.

examples.text: The Dursleys destroy the letters. Harry is tempted but held back by his ordinary life: is he truly ready to leave everything behind?
Tony flatly refuses to help: "I won't risk my daughter for this." He's found peace: why put it back on the line?
Simba wanders the desert after Mufasa's death, convinced he is guilty. Timon and Pumbaa offer him "Hakuna Matata" as an escape.

break_into_two.label: Break into Two
break_into_two.desc: The hero makes their decision and leaves the ordinary world. Entry into the adventure.
break_into_two.alert_too_early: Your break into two arrives too early. The adventure world doesn't contrast enough with the ordinary world.
break_into_two.alert_too_late: The break is too late. The transition to Act 2 is delayed and the pacing suffers.
break_into_two.alert_missing: No clear break into two identified. The passage to adventure must be a strong, active moment for the hero.

examples.text: Harry boards the Hogwarts Express with Hagrid. He chooses to enter this new world, leaving the Dursleys behind.
Tony solves the time travel equation and brings his solution to Steve. He decides to risk everything to bring back the vanished.
Simba fully embraces "Hakuna Matata" and settles into the jungle with Timon and Pumbaa, he consciously renounces his royal identity.

b_story.label: B Story
b_story.desc: Introduction of a key relationship (love, mentor, rival) that carries the story's theme.
b_story.alert_too_early: Your B story starts too early, before the main adventure is truly underway.
b_story.alert_too_late: Your B story starts too late to have sufficient impact on the hero's transformation.
b_story.alert_missing: No B story defined. A secondary storyline enriches the emotional depth of the narrative.

examples.text: The friendship with Ron and Hermione develops: two opposite mirrors who help Harry define who he is.
Thor reunites with his mother Frigga in the past. She tells him: "You don't have to be the king everyone expects." The beginning of his reconstruction.
Simba reunites with Nala, his childhood friend. She reminds him that he has an identity, a responsibility, a people waiting for him.

fun_and_games.label: Fun and Games
fun_and_games.desc: The promise of the premise is delivered. The most entertaining part.
fun_and_games.alert_too_early: The fun and games arrive too early, before the stakes and adventure world are well established.
fun_and_games.alert_too_late: The fun and games are delayed. The reader is waiting for the core action promised by the concept.
fun_and_games.alert_missing: The fun and games section is missing. This is the heart and showcase of your narrative concept.

examples.text: Magic classes, Quidditch, exploring the castle, the Mirror of Erised: Harry discovers a world that lives up to his dreams.
The time heist: New York 2012, Asgard 2013, Camp Lehigh 1970. Each jump is an adventure through MCU history.
Adult Simba lives a carefree life with Timon and Pumbaa: bug hunting, mud baths, starry nights and songs.

midpoint.label: Midpoint
midpoint.desc: False victory or false defeat that relaunches tension. Stakes are raised.
midpoint.alert_too_early: Your midpoint arrives too early. The first half will be too short and the stakes underdeveloped.
midpoint.alert_too_late: Your midpoint arrives too late. The second half's pacing will be crushed and the resolution rushed.
midpoint.alert_missing: No midpoint identified. This central pivot is essential for relaunching stakes at the halfway mark.

examples.text: Harry realizes Snape isn't the traitor and that it's Quirrell who threatens him. False lead lifted, true threat revealed.
On Titan, the Avengers nearly immobilize Thanos: false victory. Star-Lord loses his temper and everything falls apart.
Mufasa's spirit appears to Simba in the clouds: "Remember who you are." A false inner victory: Simba still hesitates.

bad_guys.label: Bad Guys Close In
bad_guys.desc: Antagonists gain the upper hand. The hero's internal flaws make them vulnerable.
bad_guys.alert_too_early: Antagonist pressure builds too quickly, before the hero has reached their peak at the midpoint.
bad_guys.alert_too_late: The antagonists don't apply pressure quickly enough after the midpoint.
bad_guys.alert_missing: The rising antagonist pressure isn't clearly marked in the narrative.

examples.text: Voldemort gets closer to the Stone, the defenses fall one by one. Quirrell actively sabotages Quidditch to eliminate Harry.
Thanos collects all the stones one by one, despite every attempt to stop him. Nothing works, the heroes pile up defeats.
Simba returns to Pride Rock but Scar reigns over devastated lands. The hyenas surround Simba, Scar holds all the power.

all_is_lost.label: All Is Lost
all_is_lost.desc: The lowest point. A major loss pushes the hero to despair.
all_is_lost.alert_too_early: Your 'All Is Lost' arrives too early. The stakes haven't had time to build sufficient intensity.
all_is_lost.alert_too_late: Your 'All Is Lost' arrives too late. The final resolution will feel rushed and less satisfying.
all_is_lost.alert_missing: No 'All Is Lost' moment. Without this nadir, the resolution will lack emotional impact.

examples.text: Harry faces Quirrell/Voldemort alone in the chamber. Trapped, with no possible rescue: all seems lost for him.
Thanos snaps his fingers. Heroes disintegrate one by one. The plan has failed. The survivors watch, powerless.
Scar publicly reveals that Simba would be responsible for Mufasa's death. Simba is on the edge of the cliff, everyone believes him guilty.

dark_night.label: Dark Night of the Soul
dark_night.desc: The hero hits rock bottom emotionally. Total questioning before resurrection.
dark_night.alert_too_early: The dark night arrives too early. The hero hasn't sunk deep enough for their rise to be meaningful.
dark_night.alert_too_late: The dark night is too late. There won't be enough room for transformation and resolution.
dark_night.alert_missing: The 'Dark Night of the Soul' is missing. Without this low point, the hero's transformation will lack credibility.

examples.text: Harry lies unconscious after the confrontation, convinced he has failed. He wakes up in the infirmary not knowing if he succeeded.
Tony, alone on his farm five years later, refuses to act: "I've found peace. I won't risk my daughter for the dead."
Simba hangs from the cliff's edge as Scar whispers the truth about Mufasa. The weight of guilt crushes everything.

break_into_three.label: Break into Three
break_into_three.desc: The hero finds the solution through a fusion of the A and B stories.
break_into_three.alert_too_early: The twist arrives too early, before the hero has truly hit rock bottom.
break_into_three.alert_too_late: The hero's revelation arrives too late to leave enough room for a satisfying resolution.
break_into_three.alert_missing: No twist or revelation identified. This is the essential engine of the final resolution.

examples.text: Dumbledore reveals to Harry that his mother's love protected him. It's not magic: it's sacrifice that makes him invincible.
Hulk/Banner brings back all the vanished with the stones. Tony then understands that the final sacrifice is his to make: "I am Iron Man."
Scar, cornered, confesses in front of everyone that he killed Mufasa. The truth frees Simba from his guilt: he can finally act.

finale.label: Finale
finale.desc: The hero applies everything they've learned to face the final ordeal and transform their world.
finale.alert_too_early: Your finale arrives too early. The hero's triumph will lack scope and development.
finale.alert_too_late: Your finale is very late. It will feel rushed or the story will seem to have dragged.

examples.text: Harry touches Quirrell and burns him through his mother's love. He triumphs not through magical power, but through what he embodies.
Tony dons the stones and snaps his fingers, knowing it will cost him his life. "I am Iron Man." He sacrifices everything for everyone.
Simba confronts Scar at the top of Pride Rock in the storm. He understands that running from his responsibility was his true crime.

final_image.label: Final Image
final_image.desc: Mirror of the opening image. Shows how much the hero and their world have changed.
final_image.alert_too_early: Your final image arrives too early. The story doesn't truly end where it should.
final_image.alert_missing: No final image. The loop with the opening image isn't closed.

examples.text: Harry, Ron and Hermione board the Hogwarts Express again. Same train, same world, but Harry is no longer the orphan under the stairs.
Steve Rogers, now aged, passes the shield to Sam. Life has run its course: the hero has found the peace he'd been seeking from the start.
Simba roars at the top of Pride Rock, his cub is presented to all the animals. Same image as the beginning: the circle of life comes full circle.

dashboard_stats.title: Coherence Score
dashboard_stats.desc: The gauge summarizes your project's overall narrative health: inconsistencies, Save the Cat structure, emotional arc… A green score means everything flows.

dashboard_inventory.title: Narrative Inventory
dashboard_inventory.desc: Your counters at a glance: characters, locations, objects, chapters, events and STC beats. A good novel typically has between 8 and 30 named characters.

dashboard_series.title: Series View
dashboard_series.desc: If your work spans multiple volumes, this table compares narrative density, structural score and inconsistencies volume by volume.

timeline_events.title: Narrative Timeline
timeline_events.desc: All your story's events in chronological order. Each column is a chapter; each card, an event with its dramatic intensity.

timeline_filters.title: Filters & Tracking
timeline_filters.desc: Filter by character (Presence or POV), by narrative thread or by dramatic outcome. Ideal for tracing a protagonist's arc chapter by chapter.

lore_tabs.title: World & Lore
lore_tabs.desc: Your world's knowledge base: characters, locations, objects and groups (factions, races, families…). Everything is browsable and editable from here.

lore_grid.title: Entity Cards
lore_grid.desc: Click a card to edit the entity. From a character card, you can open the relationship graph or navigate to related inconsistencies.

map_canvas.title: Interactive Map
map_canvas.desc: Import a background image (map of your world), then place your locations on it. Enable 'Link' mode to trace each character's journey.

map_journeys.title: Character Journeys
map_journeys.desc: Visualize each character's journey chapter by chapter. Click a location to see which characters are there at that point in the story.

stc_beats.title: Save the Cat
stc_beats.desc: The Save the Cat method breaks your story into 15 mandatory narrative beats. Each chapter is assigned to a beat to structure the dramatic arc.

stc_frise.title: Dramatic Timeline
stc_frise.desc: Visual representation of your beats over time. Diamonds indicate the ideal beat position; circles, your actual position. A large gap triggers an alert.

stc_panels.title: Alerts & Detail
stc_panels.desc: Left: structure alerts (missing beat, critical deviation). Right: detail of each beat with the associated chapter and involved entities.

heros_stages.title: Hero's Journey
heros_stages.desc: Joseph Campbell's 12 archetypal stages, organized in 3 phases: Ordinary World, Trials, Return. Select your protagonist at the top.

heros_grid.title: The 12 Stages
heros_grid.desc: Fill in the chapter and description for each stage of your character. Completed stages light up; empty ones signal an incomplete arc.

arc_chart.title: Emotional Arc
arc_chart.desc: Dramatic intensity curve chapter by chapter. Switch between Global view (all characters combined) and Characters (individual evolution by axis).

arc_graph.title: Tension Curve
arc_graph.desc: Read the peaks and valleys: good narrative rhythm alternates tension and release. A flat plateau across several chapters often signals stagnation.

plants_list.title: Narrative Setups
plants_list.desc: The plant & payoff tracker: every clue, object or promise placed in a chapter must find its resolution. Here you track their status (open, resolved, dropped).

plants_content.title: Arc & List View
plants_content.desc: Switch between List view (cards) and Arc view (SVG plant→payoff). The Arc view visually shows when each setup is planted and resolved in the timeline.

threads_list.title: Narrative Threads
threads_list.desc: Your story's subplots and secondary storylines. Create one thread per plot (romance, backstory, conspiracy…) then tag your events from the Timeline.

threads_cards.title: Thread Details
threads_cards.desc: Each thread displays its chapter range and attached events. A thread with no tagged events is an invisible subplot: consider filling it.

inc_list.title: Inconsistency Detector
inc_list.desc: Atlas automatically scans your manuscript: impossible chronology, character in the wrong place, object held by someone who doesn't exist… Click ⚡ to re-scan.

inc_severity.title: Severity Filters
inc_severity.desc: Address Critical issues first (blocking for coherence), then High. Medium and Low can wait for a proofreading pass.

home_cards.title: Your turn!
home_cards.desc: Create your own project (manual construction) or import a manuscript via your favorite AI to automatically generate timeline, lore and inconsistencies.
